claims.text: Rapid reduction kinetics promote formation of a single-phase noble-metal high-entropy alloy.
Rapid reduction kinetics promote uniform elemental mixing in the alloy.
A single-phase, uniformly mixed alloy provides a higher density of catalytically active sites.
A single-phase, uniformly mixed alloy provides a more consistent distribution of catalytically active sites.
The relevant structural mediator is a uniform atomic distribution within a single-phase alloy structure, potentially FCC.
The proposed single-phase structure has minimized phase segregation.
The proposed single-phase structure has minimized defects.
A faster reduction rate kinetically traps a metastable, well-mixed high-entropy phase.
Faster reduction limits diffusion during material formation.
Homogeneous elemental mixing enables inter-element synergistic interactions at catalytic sites.
Inter-element synergistic interactions optimize the electronic properties of active sites.
Optimized active-site electronic properties enhance catalytic performance.
Fast-reduction samples will have a more homogeneous elemental distribution than slow-reduction samples.
Fast-reduction samples will exhibit better catalytic activity, such as higher turnover frequency or lower overpotential, than slow-reduction samples.
Slow reduction allows more time for phase segregation.
Slow reduction promotes formation of structurally heterogeneous products.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials made by solution-phase reduction under typical laboratory temperature and atmosphere controls.
The reduction-rate threshold for optimal uniformity and catalytic performance depends on alloy composition and catalytic reaction conditions.
